submissions.title: Boise City Council approves 6-month moratorium on large data center construction
submissions.excerpt: temporarily prohibit new data centre developments measuring more than 100,000 sqft or requiring more than 20 megawatts of power
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Boise, Idaho City Council voted unanimously on 2026-11-10 to enact an emergency 6-month moratorium on large data center construction within city limits, triggered by projects over 100,000 sqft or drawing more than 20 MW. Purpose: time to review code, water, energy, wastewater, noise and public-safety impacts before accepting or processing new applications meeting those thresholds. Not tied to a specific tracked project -- this is a future-siting barrier, not a project-level event. Same caveat as above re: WebFetch being unavailable in this session to byte-verify the quoted ordinance language against the article.

submissions.title: Edmond City Council extends moratorium on new data centers through June
submissions.excerpt: extend the city's existing moratorium on data centers through June 30, 2027
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Edmond, Oklahoma City Council voted unanimously on 2026-11-09 to extend its existing data center moratorium (originally Ordinance 4091, enacted June 2026) through 2027-06-30. The pause covers acceptance of rezoning and building-permit applications enabling construction, expansion or operation of data centers citywide. Not tied to a specific tracked project. Distinct from the separate Oklahoma City (not Edmond) moratorium extension reported in the same news cycle -- do not conflate the two municipalities. Same WebFetch-unavailable caveat as the other findings in this batch.
